CSE Global appoints Amitava Guharoy as lead independent director
article:
CSE Global (SGX:544 ) announced that it has appointed Amitava Guharoy as its new lead independent director. His appointment will take effect from Aug 10.

Apart from his position as the lead independent director, Guharoy will also be taking on the role of Chairman of CSE Global’s audit and risk committee (ARC) and member of the nominating committee (NC).

As part of the selection process, the NC has engaged Singapore Institute of Directors to assist in identifying suitable candidates for the NC’s consideration.

“In considering this appointment, the Board took into account, in particular, Guharoy’s extensive financial and accounting expertise and substantial experience in audit, M&A and corporate finance,” CSE Global states in the Aug 7 announcement.

CSE Global’s previous lead independent director, Tan Chian Khong, who has been on the board for seven years, stepped down back on June 2. In his resignation filing, CSE Global states that it was due to the “differences of views with regard to working with controlling shareholders”.

Based on CSE Global’s latest annual report, Heliconia Capital Management, a subsidiary of Temasek Holdings, is the single largest controlling shareholder with a 23.79% stake.

See also: Cushman & Wakefield appoints Zeïna Henni to lead Singapore project and development services

CSE Global is currently undertaking a strategic review “with the objective of maximising shareholder value”, following a request from its controlling shareholder. The company issued a follow up announcement back on Aug 5 that the strategic review is still ongoing.

Shares in CSE Global closed 1 cent higher, or 0.8% up at $1.26 on Aug 7.

title: Aspial Lifestyle reports 89% y-o-y rise in net profit to $55 mil on record $464.2 mil revenue for 1HFY2026
article:
For 1HFY2026 ended June 30, net profit for Aspial Lifestyle surged 89% y-o-y to $55 million, with revenue rising 26% y-o-y to a record $464.2 million. The company has declared an interim dividend of 0.9 cents, which is 125% higher than 1HFY2025.

Gross profit margin improved by 210 basis points to 38.7% from 1HFY2025’s 36.6%. Excluding $5.2 million of gold hedging loss, Aspial Lifestyle’s underlying profitability would have been higher.

All three business segments saw growth. Retail revenue increased 25.2% y-o-y to $399.6 million; pawnbroking revenue rose 29.3% y-o-y to $55.3 million as the pledge book saw sustained growth; and revenue for secured lending revenue grew 76.1% to $9.2 million, attributed to the firm’s BigFundr platform.

In May, Aspial Lifestyle raised $84.8 million from a placement of 211 million new shares. This, combined with “strong” earnings, helped the company to improve its net debt-to-equity ratio to 1.7 times as at end-June from 2.1 times as at end-December 2025. The company held cash and equivalents of $82.6 million against interest nearing loans of $104.5 million and medium term notes of $179.3 million.

Aspial Lifestyle operated 118 stores across six brands in Singapore, Malaysia and selected international markets as of June 30. Its MAS-licensed secured lending platform, BigFundr, continued to scale, with funds under management increasing by more than 25% from Dec 31, 2025.

During the first-half of the year, Aspial Lifestyle acquired the remaining equity interests in its Malaysian pawnbroking joint venture, achieving full ownership of its Malaysia operations. The company expects this development to help accelerate the expansion of its pawnbroking and retail network in Malaysia.

See also: Fraser and Neave reports 9MFY2026 earnings of $177.1 mil, 4.5% higher y-o-y

The company also completed its move from the Catalist-board to Mainboard of the Singapore stock exchange. It says that it remains confident in the long-term fundamentals of its business despite market volatility caused by global macroeconomic uncertainties, geopolitical developments and gold price fluctuations. Aspial Lifestyle’s board remains optimistic for the full year performance of the company.

Shares in Aspial Lifestyle closed unchanged at 38 cents on Aug 7.
